pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: drm/fb_helper: Add drm_fb_helper functions to manage fb_info creation Every drm driver calls framebuffer_alloc, fb_alloc_cmap, unregister_framebuffer, fb_dealloc_cmap and framebuffer_release in order to emulate fbdev support. Create drm_fb_helper functions that perform the above operations. This is part of an effort to prevent drm drivers from calling fbdev functions directly. It also removes repetitive code from drivers. There are some drivers that call alloc_apertures after framebuffer_alloc and some that don't. Make the helper always call alloc_apertures. This would make certain drivers allocate memory for apertures but not use them. Since it's a small amount of memory, it shouldn't be an issue. v2: - Added kerneldocs - Added a check for non-NULL fb_helper before proceeding. This will make the helpers work when we have a module param for fbdev emulation Signed-off-by: Archit Taneja <architt@codeaurora.org> Signed-off-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch> (cherry picked from commit b8017d6c33be9862505a9154e302c4b00cbfca43) Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chrome-os-partner:43252 TEST=Build and boot a recovery image and verify has UI (per instructions in crosbug.com/p/43252) Change-Id: Iba69c579a30fac40719cceae7bb88592c5e17e34 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/329854 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm: Add top level Kconfig option for DRM fbdev emulation Legacy fbdev emulation support via DRM is achieved through KMS FB helpers. Most modesetting drivers enable provide fbdev emulation by default by selecting KMS FB helpers. A few provide a separate Kconfig option for the user to enable or disbale fbdev emulation. Enabling fbdev emulation is finally a distro-level decision. Having a top level Kconfig option for fbdev emulation helps by providing a uniform way to enable/disable fbdev emulation for any modesetting driver. It also lets us remove unnecessary driver specific Kconfig options that causes bloat. With a top level Kconfig in place, we can stub out the fb helper functions when not needed without breaking functionality. Having stub functions also prevents drivers to require wrapping fb helper function calls with #ifdefs. DRM_FBDEV_EMULATION defaults to y since many drivers enable fbdev emulation by default and majority of distributions expect the fbdev interface in the kernel. BUG=chrome-os-partner:43252 TEST=Build and boot a recovery image and verify has UI (per instructions in crosbug.com/p/43252) Signed-off-by: Archit Taneja <architt@codeaurora.org> Signed-off-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch> (cherry picked from commit a03fdcb1863297481a4b817c2a759cafcbdfa0ae) Change-Id: Id948ac96a30b2457acc484f65d8b97300abadbbe Signed-off-by: CK Hu <ck.hu@mediatek.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/330050 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: ARM: Add a debugfs file for dumping CP14/CP15 regs In order to confirm that certain errata have been applied properly, we'd like to be able to read some CP14 / CP15 registers from userspace. Normally that's not allowed, but for some registers there's no harm in providing read-only access to userspace. Let's add a bit of infrastructure here for doing this. For now we'll only add one register: one that's needed for confirming an errata has been applied properly on A12 / A17. BUG=chrome-os-partner:50137 TEST=taskset -c $i cat /sys/kernel/debug/arm_coprocessor_debug Change-Id: Ib4685e505ae0411d2dd3e94a0785b5f470523f29 Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/329960 Reviewed-by: Olof Johansson <olofj@chromium.org>

kernel_CheckArmErrata: Add new test to check for ARM errata We recently enabled an ARM Erratum for Cortex-A12. We want to make sure that this errata doesn't get lost, even if we later decide to rebase to a new kernel or we rejitter our configs. Let's add a test to make sure that the erratum fix is present. Note that to test this we need some coprocessor registers that aren't usually present from userspace, so this depends on a kernel change. If we detect that we're on an errata-ridden processor but don't have the needed kernel infrastructure to check for errata, the test will fail. This test is designed to support checking for the presence of more errata on future ARM processors assuming that they can be checked for using similar methods. CQ-DEPEND=CL:Ib4685e505ae0411d2dd3e94a0785b5f470523f29 BUG=chrome-os-partner:50137 TEST=test_that kernel_CheckArmErrata and kernel_CheckArmErrata.doctest Change-Id: I9fbb6f73a8c62886d59753be6223983b1b2c650f Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/329950 Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

gooftool: Keep simple __init__ to avoid dependency cycle. When importing modules, Python need to solve all modules included by __init__. Previously we put the main implementation of Gooftool in its __init__.py, which makes modules interacting with Gooftool (i.e., hwid) will have problem due to dependency cycle. To prevent that, we should follow Python guide line to make __init__ a simple zero dummy file and move the implementation details to a new 'core.py', with the command line and command interface (gooftool.py) into 'commands.py'. This helps resolving dependency issues and makes it easier for people to figure out the difference between 'gooftool/__init__.py#Gooftool' and 'gooftool/gooftool.py'. BUG=none TEST=make test; gooftool Change-Id: If207bcb6e42bf9a99954c2be23d40e39c13bbfae Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/329489 Commit-Ready: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org>

Fix import error "AttributeError: 'module' object has no attribute 'factory'" It is found that on some environments (i.e., a fresh checkout of public repo and totally build from source, and the first time run build_packages), programs importing other modules in the form "import a.b as c" would lead to AttributeError when making factory bundle. The reason is "import a.b as c" will need to first inject 'b' into existing name space a, which will become a problem if a is not initialized yet (for instance, if the one imports a.b was actually pulled in by a's own dependency or if the modules in sys.modules was explicitly modified). The correct form is to do "from a import b as c", which only resolves sys.modules and no need to worry about the name space problem. Reference: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/24807434/ . BUG=none TEST=make test; make bundle Change-Id: I8550e55ef98c5322228f3229ad3012cafcf4cc96 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/329833 Commit-Ready: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wei-Ning Huang <wnhuang@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mali: drm_reservation_cb_done after reservation_object_add_shared_fence In general it looks like it's wise to call reservation_object_add_shared_fence() _before_ calling drm_reservation_cb_done(). The difference should really only matter on PREEMPT kernels since drm_reservation_cb_done() can only ever do schedule_work() which should do nothing until we give up the current CPU (unless PREEMPT). Said another way: before PREEMPT the two orderings were equivalent. Now they're not. Right now we don't have PREEMPT enabled on 3.8, but it's still good to fix this. In this particular case presumably the callback could somehow end up NULLing out "katom->rendered_fence" and we'd end up with the same type of problem that we fixed in ("drm: rockchip: Add the shared fence before calling the callback"). In testing we haven't seen the katom->rendered_fence actually become NULL, but it seems better not to tempt fate. BUG=chromium:586711 TEST=See steps in bug Change-Id: I597cc7060acd069c1fce6bc5d9a137b584a3d24d Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/329402 Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>
